atoms.text: Welcome back everyone! It’s going to be another busy school year, and the academic calendar is looking very full! In just a few weeks, we are hosting a careers fair for all students. After that, the term will be fairly quiet until the Christmas period, where there will be lots of activities and events to go to, such as the Christmas play.

b: something that happens once a year
another name for the Christmas holidays
++a period of time in the school year
a type of venue for performances

atoms.a: What is the first event of the school year?

trainers.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: In the second term, you will have some mock exams in the first week of February. These help to track your progress and prepare for future exams, so it’s very important to revise for them. In the first week after half term, you will have parents’ evening. The term will finish for the Easter holidays at the end of March.

atoms.text: The summer term also has lots on offer. Like every year, the school band is hosting its annual charity concert in May. Sports day will be in June, and all students must choose which events they would like to compete in. Finally, just before we finish for the summer, you will have your individual and year group photos.

b: something that happens once a month

atoms.a: Which event will only some students take part in?
How many terms are there altogether in the school year?

atoms.sound: What extracurricular activities are you going to do this year? I usually join the gardening club, but I think I want to try something new this term.
Well... I organise the chess club, so I’m always there, and I want to try some baking as well. I usually play football too, but I won’t have time to play this term.
I feel the same! I’m still going to edit the school newspaper, but I’ll only have time for one extra club, and I really want to get better at guitar, so I will probably take music lessons.
Do you have any advice for choosing clubs? I want to join something, but I’m nervous about trying something new.
That’s understandable, but they’re a great way to socialise and have fun. I would suggest joining a club with friends or people you know, so it won’t seem as scary.
You could also join a club that matches your favourite subjects, so it feels less challenging. Which classes do you like?
Hmm ... that makes sense! Well I love my drama classes, so I think I will give the movie and drama club a go. Thanks!
